key_insight: This paper investigates whether LLM agents can automate checks of scientific reproducibility and analytical robustness using cancer-registry research as a case study. The provided abstract is truncated, so it does not establish how well the agents performed.
problem_solved: Reproducing published findings and checking whether conclusions withstand analytical changes require costly manual effort, limiting systematic evaluation of scientific reliability.
method: Study LLM agents as tools for automating reproduction and robustness analysis.
Ground the evaluation in research using SEER, a widely used U.S. cancer registry.
Introduce SEER-Repro, a benchmark for evaluating reproduction; its full composition and results are unavailable in the provided excerpt.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work frames scientific verification as a concrete agent-evaluation task. It could help guide tools that reduce manual review effort, though effectiveness cannot be assessed from the excerpt.
visual_elements: Workflow: published study → LLM agent → reproduction and robustness checks.

paper_title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
paper_authors: Shicheng Liu, Krista Opsahl-Ong, Andrew Drozdov, Julian Killingback, Arnav Singhvi
